A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same research work, Calibrating Expressions of Certainty. All main-text and appendix pages are readable, and the methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original radiologist-calibration analyses using 2,662 paired radiology reports, language-model experiments on SciQ and TruthfulQA, extraction accuracies, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds descriptive analyses of diagnostic certainty-phrase frequencies, including variation across radiologists.

M1.justification: The distribution-based confidence representation, calibration estimators, and optimal-transport calibration procedure remain unchanged. The revised mean-estimator expression is mathematically equivalent; new extraction examples and applicability explanations do not introduce method components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same paired radiology-report dataset, SciQ, and TruthfulQA for the same tasks. Appendix B.1 in v2 provides more information about the existing radiology cohort, rather than introducing another dataset or population.

E2.justification: Platt scaling and histogram binning retain the same comparison rows in Table 1. The evaluated language models and the survey, on-the-fly, and fixed-distribution comparisons in Table 3 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, evaluation sample sizes, model versions, metrics, binning settings, and calibration hyperparameters remain unchanged. The newly stated 12-hour report-pairing criterion and explicit zero-shot description document existing experiments rather than report protocol revisions.

E4.justification: New Figures 5–6 examine which certainty phrases occur in radiology reports and how their usage varies across radiologists. These add limited descriptive analyses; the existing phrase-set, transport-hyperparameter, and binning-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 retains bootstrap resampling with 100 samples and 95% confidence intervals. Existing uncertainty displays are unchanged, and the added frequency analyses introduce no reported significance tests, run counts, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds aggregate and radiologist-specific phrase-frequency results in Figures 5–6, alongside descriptive cohort statistics. Scores in Tables 1, 3, and 4 and results in all matched existing plots are unchanged; there is no new benchmark performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 Equation (7) rewrites the mean estimator from v1 Equation (6) using an equivalent product of bin probability and conditional expectation. Proposition 1, the calibration derivations, and Appendix A proofs are retained without substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusions retain the same central contributions: distribution-valued certainty phrases, generalized calibration estimation and visualization, and interpretable optimal-transport calibration. Emphasizing competitive performance and natural-language outputs restates the original claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly acknowledges that radiologists’ receptiveness and ability to adopt calibration suggestions require clinical investigation. Appendix D clarifies that additional phrases need quantified meanings and that free-form text requires a classification framing for calibration assessment.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds cohort-selection and preprocessing details, including adult eligibility, 12-hour pairing, report-section extraction, de-identification, and terminology normalization. v2 also clarifies zero-shot prompting and adds a GitHub code link. These expand documentation and access information without establishing implementation changes.

R1.justification: The related-work section and bibliography retain the same works and research positioning. Expanded discussion of scalar-score methods reiterates the existing distinction that the proposed method directly produces certainty phrases.

P1.justification: Section 5 becomes Discussions with limitations and conclusions; Appendix B gains dataset and usage-example subsections, and Appendix D adds FAQs. Local paragraph rewrites and explanatory additions improve exposition while preserving most of the original narrative and structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds two frequency plots and two boxed usage examples, revises Table 1’s caption and highlighting, and improves the estimator equation layout. Existing figures are retained with renumbering and reflow, alongside conference headers.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through dataset-preparation details and code-access information, while Section 5 explicitly acknowledges that clinician uptake remains untested. The added examples and FAQ clarify the method’s interpretation and applicability. These are useful, focused improvements; the central method, proofs, and comparative performance evidence remain unchanged.
